- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward bias — add 2–5% to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, model tends to overcorrect — dampen the final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.3–0.6) and forecast diverges from history, align forecast mean to recent 7-day average to reduce lag.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, adjust next forecast to reflect mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
